From increasing order \(1,\ldots,m,k,N\), let \(p=N/k\). Since \(k\) is the second largest divisor, \(p\) is the second smallest divisor, hence prime, and \(p\le k\).

But
\[
p=\frac{N}{k}=\frac{k^k+m^m}{k}=k^{k-1}+\frac{m^m}{k}.
\]
If \(k\ge 3\), then \(p>k^{k-1}\ge k\), contradicting \(p\le k\). Thus \(k=2\). Then \(m=1\), so
\[
N=2^2+1^1=5,
\]
but \(2\) is not a divisor of \(5\), contradiction.

Therefore no such positive integer \(N\) exists.

\[
\boxed{\text{No such } N \text{ exists}}
\]
